description: Chain level joint translation. A chain is translated as one unit: its members are merged into a single source text, that text is translated whole, and the translation is cut back into one piece per member. Everything the two halves of that round trip need is declared here. join says how two consecutive members are put back together, and records the separator it used so the merge can be read back. profiles say what a sentence end looks like in the target language and where a cut may legally land in it; the profile is chosen by the target language tag, longest declared prefix first, falling back to the default. strategies say which redistribution a chain is cut by, read from the endpoint pair class the chain was built under, never from a page type or a publication. A body chain is cut on sentence boundaries and falls back to a proportional cut only for the members no boundary is left for; a display line chain has no sentence structure to cut on and is proportional throughout. Every cut is a position in the translated string and nothing but the one page break hyphen is ever added or removed, so the pieces always join back to exactly the translation that came in. Punctuation is written as JSON unicode escapes to keep this file ASCII.

join.description: How consecutive members are merged. A member whose last character is a trailing hyphen is a word the page break cut in half, so the hyphen is dropped and the halves close up; the hyphen is kept when it stands alone as a word, which is what the preceding character being a space tells us. Two members that meet where neither side is written with interword spaces close up as well: spaceless_script_ranges lists the code point ranges, low..high in hexadecimal, whose scripts set no space between words. Everything else takes the default separator. Nothing else is added to or removed from a member.

profiles.description: One sentence model per target script. terminators end a sentence wherever they stand. space_gated_terminators end one only when whitespace or the end of the text follows, which is what keeps a decimal point, a version number and an in-word full stop from ending a sentence; the two lists together must not be empty. closers are the marks stripped after a terminator before the gate is read, so a quoted sentence still ends where the quotation does. A run of terminators is one boundary and the last character of the run decides whether the gate applies. sentence_min_chars is the shortest sentence a boundary may close, counted in non-space characters: below it the boundary is dropped and the text carries on into the next sentence, which is what absorbs single letter initials. It is bounded by the range the flat sentence_min_chars declares. break_rule says where a proportional cut may land: word_boundary only after whitespace, any_char anywhere a combining sequence is not broken. language_prefixes match the target language tag, longest first; a prefix may be declared by one profile only.

strategies.description: Which redistribution a chain is cut by, keyed by the endpoint pair class the chain was built under in chain_detection.json. sentence_greedy assigns whole sentences to members by their share of the source and cuts proportionally only where no sentence boundary is left, which it reports as a proportional fallback. proportional cuts by share throughout and claims no sentence structure. A pair class not named here takes the default.
